messages:
maya: Observed spike in soft 429s on continuous-batcher canary yesterday evening. Profiler shows weird kernel selection when kv_hit_rate > 0.7 — microbatches collapse to size 1-2 and token budget gets burned quickly. Posting snippet and rough numbers.

oliver: Can you paste the profiler/snippet and the admission decision log?

maya: Sure — here's the relevant extract from the canary logs and batcher trace:
```
batch_formation: [1,1,2,1,3,1]
kv_hit_rate: 0.78
seq_len_p50: 128
kernel_hint_selected: matmul_fast_fp16
token_budget_before: 12000
token_budget_after: 982
admission_decision: soft_reject
reason: budget_estimate_mismatch_due_kv_savings
```

sara: Huh. Looks like the token budget calc isn't discounting KV hits properly. If a request has high kv_hit, effective token cost should be reduced. Also prefetch window might be evicting usable prefixes.

kai: Reminder — last week I changed the kernel hint heuristic to prefer low-latency kernels for short seqs; maybe that interacts badly with the batch assembler when kv hits produce shorter remaining lengths. Could be a kernel mismatch + budget mis-estimate.

maya: Action suggestions: 1) temporarily apply kv_hit_discount=0.5 in token_budget calc 2) shrink prefetch window from 128 -> 64 for the canary 3) emit per-batch kernel_choice histograms and batch-assembly timeline for 1% traffic.

oliver: :thumbsup: I'll push a canary with those tweaks (1% traffic), monitor soft429s, p50/p95 latency, and batch-size distribution. ETA ~20m.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Triggered canary deploy r/eng-runtime#4345 -> canary (batcher-kv-discount). Logs: https://internal.redwood/canary/4345

sara: Add a debug flag to the batcher that emits timestamps for enqueue -> assemble -> kernel_call so we can correlate kernel selection timing.

kai: Caution: if kv_discount is too aggressive we might over-admit and increase latency SLO breaches. Start at 1% and keep a 0.1% rollback hook. Also add smoothing to avoid oscillation.

maya: Agreed. Start 1% -> 5% if stable for 30m. I'll create a replay harness to run 1h of production traces against the change.

oliver: Ran a short replay on the harness: soft429s dropped ~60% on the canary, batch sizes stabilized (median 4 -> 5), p95 latency increased ~10ms. Charts uploaded: https://internal.redwood/reports/batcher_canary_4345

maya: Nice lift. Proposal: make kv_discount adaptive: kv_discount = 0.3 + 0.7 * kv_hit_rate, capped [0.1, 0.8], and add 30s hysteresis on updates. That should balance over-admit risk.

kai: I'll prototype that formula and include exponential smoothing (alpha=0.2) on kv_hit_rate estimates.

deploy-bot: canary metrics snapshot: soft429_rate 0.40 -> 0.15, p95 latency 120ms -> 130ms, cpu_util unchanged. Full metrics: https://internal.redwood/metrics/4345

maya: OK next steps: merge PR for token budget changes + batch telemetry, run 24h canary, then run a kernel-selection microbenchmark matrix to ensure we didn't regress kernel throughput. If stable, promote to 10% then 100%.

oliver: PR opened: r/eng-runtime #987 - "kv-aware token budget + batch telemetry"

sara: Thanks. If we promote, please file a short postmortem template in eng-sre and tag us for rollback runbooks.

kai: One more note — we should add a metric for "effective_tokens_saved_by_kv" so cost accounting stays accurate.

maya: Good call. I'll add that to the telemetry PR.

oliver: Summary: canary shows promising reduction in soft 429s, slight p95 latency increase, plan is conservative rollout with adaptive kv_discount and smoothing.

sara: ✅ keep an eye on kernel_choice histograms; if matmul_fast_fp16 continues to be picked for high-kv batches we may need a kernel-hint override path.

maya: Will follow up with the harness replay results and tags. Thanks all.
